hints: Focus on how properties change down Group 2, reactivity, solubility and thermal stability all follow clear trends.
The sulfate clue is the easiest start, solubility of sulfates decreases down the group so the most soluble one must be at the top.
Use the hydroxide and carbonate clues to order the rest, X is above W and Z is below W, so W must be stuck in the middle.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 2 trends down the group**

Reactivity with acid increases down. Hydroxide solubility increases down. Sulfate solubility decreases down. Carbonate thermal stability increases down, so lower carbonates decompose more slowly.

Trend summary:
$$\text{Mg at top} \rightarrow \text{Ca} \rightarrow \text{Sr} \rightarrow \text{Ba at bottom}$$

**Identify Y from the sulfate clue**

The sulfate of Y is the most soluble of the four. Since sulfates get less soluble down the group, the most soluble must be the top element.

So:
$$Y = \text{magnesium, Mg}$$

**Place W, X and Z in order**

W reacts faster than Y, so W is below Mg, as expected. Hydroxide of X is less soluble than hydroxide of W, so hydroxides are more soluble down, meaning X is above W. Carbonate of Z decomposes more slowly than carbonate of W, so stability increases down, meaning Z is below W.

So from top to bottom:
$$Y (\text{Mg}) > X > W > Z$$

**Deduce W is strontium and calculate its nitrate $M_r$**

The only order for Ca, Sr, Ba that fits X above W above Z is X = Ca, W = Sr, Z = Ba. The nitrate is $\text{Sr(NO}_3)_2$.

$$M_r = 87.6 + 2 \times (14.0 + 3 \times 16.0) = 87.6 + 124.0 = 211.6$$

options.A: 148.3 is the $M_r$ of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ ($24.3 + 124.0$). This is the nitrate of Y, the most soluble sulfate, not W.
options.B: 164.1 is the $M_r$ of $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ ($40.1 + 124.0$). This is the nitrate of X, whose hydroxide is less soluble than that of W, so it sits above W.
options.C: 211.6 is the $M_r$ of $\text{Sr(NO}_3)_2$ ($87.6 + 124.0$). All four clues place Sr in the middle position as W, above Ba and below Ca and Mg.
options.D: 261.3 is the $M_r$ of $\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2$ ($137.3 + 124.0$). This is the nitrate of Z, whose carbonate is most stable and decomposes most slowly, so it sits below W.
